architecture.mechanism: Gradual integration of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices, neural networks, and sound analysis to detect and predict accidental carrier bearing damage on an assembly conveyor without per-roller sensor installation.
architecture.intervention: Retrofit the existing 4000-roller conveyor plant with a sparse network of IIoT acoustic edge nodes mounted at fixed plant positions (e.g., support structures, transfer points, walkways) that continuously capture audio from multiple rollers simultaneously; transmit streams to a central processor running neural-network-based anomaly detection trained to identify characteristic bearing-seizure acoustic signatures, while using known roller positions and acoustic propagation models to localize the affected roller.
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of incipient bearing wear/seizure on any of the 4000 rollers without installing contact sensors on each roller, achieved at low per-roller retrofit cost, with no production downtime and a false-alarm rate held under 2 percent per month through neural-network discrimination of bearing faults from plant ambient noise.
architecture.falsification_test: Install the IIoT acoustic + neural-network system on a representative conveyor section containing at least 200 rollers, induce controlled early-stage bearing wear on 10 rollers over 90 days, and measure (a) detection latency before failure, (b) false-alarm rate per month, (c) per-roller retrofit cost averaged across the fleet, and (d) installation-related downtime; the intervention fails if false-alarm rate exceeds 2 percent per month, per-roller cost exceeds $15, or any installation step requires halting production.
